crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Protein Structure Prediction
children.blurb: Protein structure prediction uses machine learning to estimate the three-dimensional shape of a protein from its amino acid sequence.

children.name: Designing New Molecules
children.blurb: Designing new molecules with AI covers computational generation and evaluation of candidate chemical structures for drug discovery, including small molecules, peptides, and biologics.

children.name: Simulated Clinical Trials
children.blurb: Simulated clinical trials use computational models of patients, diseases, and treatments to predict how a drug might perform before or instead of a traditional human trial.

children.name: Toxicity Forecasting
children.blurb: Toxicity forecasting uses machine learning to predict whether a candidate molecule will cause harm in a biological system before it enters costly laboratory or animal testing.

children.name: Drug Repurposing
children.blurb: Drug repurposing is the practice of finding new therapeutic uses for medicines that are already approved or have passed early safety testing.

sections.body: Drug discovery and molecular simulation is the use of computational methods, including AI, to find and test potential medicines before lab work and human trials. AI models now predict protein structures from sequence data, propose new molecules with desired properties, estimate toxicity, and simulate parts of clinical trials. They also scan existing drugs for new uses, a process called repurposing. This site tracks 800 scientific models, which shows how much of the work has moved from handcrafted rules to learned patterns. The aim is not to replace wet labs or clinicians but to narrow the search space and flag candidates worth testing. In practice, AI is a screening and design assistant, not an autonomous discoverer.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are relatively mature. Protein structure prediction has become a standard first step for many research groups, though predicted structures are not always perfect and can miss dynamic behavior. Molecule generation can produce plausible candidates, but synthesizing them and showing they work in living systems remains hard. Simulated clinical trials can explore hypotheses, yet they do not substitute for real trials with real patients. Toxicity forecasting is useful for early filtering, but it often fails on rare effects and diverse populations. Drug repurposing has produced leads, but confirming benefit still requires rigorous clinical evidence, and the honest limit is that AI speeds up parts of the pipeline while the slow, expensive, and uncertain parts remain.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section follow the pipeline from target to candidate. Protein Structure Prediction explains how models infer three dimensional shapes from sequence, which helps identify binding sites. Designing New Molecules covers generative and optimization methods that propose compounds with desired properties. Simulated Clinical Trials looks at how models try to estimate safety and efficacy before or alongside real studies. Toxicity Forecasting focuses on predicting harmful effects early, while Drug Repurposing examines how existing medicines are screened for new indications. A reader can move through these pages in order to see where AI helps, where it only assists, and where human experiments still decide.
